clue.text: Just out of one's sight, out of one's mind?

definitions.meaning: something that has gone past a curve in the road can no longer be seen
an informal British idiom for crazy or mad

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally places something past a curve and hidden, and idiomatically means driven crazy.

clue.text: Different, as opposed to Him from the New Testament?

parts.words: as opposed to Him from the New Testament
parts.note: the counterpart of the New Testament is the Old Testament, abbreviated OT

parts.words: as opposed to Him from the New Testament
parts.note: the feminine counterpart of the pronoun Him is her

explanation.surface: A theological contrast between God in the New Testament and some different deity.
explanation.walkthrough: Each part is flipped to its opposite: New Testament becomes Old (OT) and Him becomes her.
explanation.definitionFit: Other is a standard synonym for different, as in 'some other day'.

clue.text: Queen into arnica, I suspect, as a plant

indicators.note: used as an adjective meaning doubtful, it tells us the letters are not to be trusted in their order

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A herbalist slipping the Queen into an arnica remedy, doubting it as a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is only a link here: ER, ARNICA and I are all shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: Cineraria is a daisy-family flowering plant often grown in pots.

clue.text: Worker on boat needs handle to hold when reversing

indicators.note: the words read backwards in sequence, so the joined pieces are turned round together

parts.note: a handle is slang for a name
to grab is to seize and hold

explanation.surface: A deckhand needs something to grip while backing the vessel up.
explanation.walkthrough: NAMEGRAB read backwards gives BARG plus EMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargeman is someone employed on a barge, a flat-bottomed river boat.

clue.text: Coquette, one using a comb?

definitions.meaning: a flirt who leads others on without intending to follow through
backcombing hair to give it volume is called teasing it

explanation.definitionFit: A tease is a flirt, and someone backcombing hair is literally teasing it.

clue.text: Case where small, small animals carried around by writer

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: being carried by something puts these letters inside it
joins the carried letters to the thing holding them

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: turned around, so the animals' letters run backwards

parts.note: mice are small rodents

explanation.surface: A box in which tiny creatures are carted about by an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like a container but is the definition, in the sense of an instance; 'around' turns the animals backwards (ECIM) before the writer carries them.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is an example or instance, just as one speaks of a case of something.

clue.text: Some money tossed over for cheese-maker's substance

indicators.note: flipped over end to end, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tenner is a British ten-pound note, some money

explanation.surface: Coins flipped to pay for a cheese ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: A TENNER is British slang for a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Rennet is the enzyme preparation used to curdle milk in making cheese.

clue.text: Chic, flash hunk

parts.note: a flash is a moment, informally a mo
an attractive man is called a dish or a hunk

explanation.surface: A stylish, showy, good-looking man.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is British informal for a moment ('half a mo').
explanation.definitionFit: Modish means fashionable, the same as chic.

clue.text: Pockets girl filled with drink

indicators.note: the girl's name has the drink packed inside it

parts.note: Maria is a girl's name
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A girl's pockets stuffed with alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsupia are the pouches of marsupials, a zoological word for pockets.

clue.text: Boom crushing me, I move around

indicators.note: the booming noise squeezes the other word into its middle

parts.note: a boom is a loud roar

explanation.surface: A loud noise flattening me as I wander about.
explanation.definitionFit: A roamer is a wanderer, one who could say of themselves that they move around.

clue.text: Reduced prize money — that was a dip

parts.note: reduced means cut
a purse is the prize money in a boxing match or race

explanation.surface: A trimmed prize fund described as a slump.
explanation.walkthrough: A dip is slang for a pickpocket, so the definition describes an old-time thief.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutpurse was a historical pickpocket, who cut purses from belts, as a dip does.

clue.text: Brusque tip for final candidates

parts.note: brusque means curt or short
to tip is to lean or list

explanation.surface: A curt piece of advice for the last applicants.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortlist is the selected group of finalists for a job or prize.

clue.text: Child carriers: some require tubes, reversible

indicators.note: the run is to be read backwards
some of the letters, a run taken from inside the words

explanation.surface: Something about baby carriers needing tubes and being reversible.
explanation.walkthrough: The run IRETU inside 'require tubes', read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Wombs carry unborn children; this is the plural of the Latin word for womb.

clue.text: Toe-curling lament about wig then, or otherwise

indicators.note: the lament goes around the rearranged letters

parts.note: to lament is to cry

indicators.note: in another way, signalling the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An embarrassing complaint about a wig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lament' looks like part of the definition but supplies the outer letters; 'otherwise' rearranges wig, then and or into INGEWORTH, which the cry goes 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cringeworthy is so embarrassing it makes one's toes curl.

clue.text: Diamond ring hunted on motorway, all kicking off on public transport

indicators.note: every one of these words gives only its starting letter

parts.note: a bus is public transport

explanation.surface: A diamond ring hunted down on the motorway, then everyone starting a fight on a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhombus is the geometric diamond shape, an equal-sided parallelogram.

clue.text: Legendary King Arthur opened case of Gawain being unruly

indicators.note: out of order and disorderly, so the letters are mixed
the outer letters, like a case around the word

explanation.surface: King Arthur unlocking a box belonging to Sir Gawain, who is misbehaving.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur is part of the fodder here; Uther was Arthur's father in legend.
explanation.definitionFit: In Arthurian legend he is the king who fathered Arthur.

clue.text: Sad song awful, good to intervene

indicators.note: to come between, putting the letter inside the other word

parts.note: dire means awful

explanation.surface: A terrible sad song that a good singer must step in to rescue.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful song or lament for the dead.

clue.text: Particular measures taken initially, about which he is concerned

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the concern goes around the letter

parts.note: cares means is concerned

indicators.note: only the starting letter of the word

explanation.surface: Specific measures, first taken, that a man is worried about.
explanation.walkthrough: HE CARES 'about' T, which is the start of 'taken'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hectares are particular metric units for measuring land area.

clue.text: Row in the Treasury

definitions.meaning: a row or tier, as of oars or switches
a place where money is held, a financial institution

explanation.definitionFit: A bank is both a row of things and a store of money.

clue.text: First of eight missing, seven reels roughly collected

indicators.note: approximately arranged, so the letters are jumbled
the opening letter of the word
the letter is absent from the jumbled pool

explanation.surface: A film missing reel one, with seven reels roughly gathered.
explanation.walkthrough: SEVEN REELS minus E is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerveless means calm and composed, just as collected does.

clue.text: Here, polish has faded, for example?

parts.note: being here means being present
to polish something is to perfect it

explanation.surface: In this place, a polish that has lost its shine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has faded' is a verb in the tense formed with has or have plus a past participle.
explanation.definitionFit: The grammar tense formed with has plus a past participle, as in this example.

clue.text: Ape that can fly

definitions.meaning: to ape is to mimic, a verb

explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to copy someone's words, and the bird itself flies.

clue.text: Copper prices not to be tampered with

indicators.note: meddled with, so the letters are interfered with and rearranged

explanation.surface: Fixed prices that must not be altered.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is slang for a police officer, and an inspector is a police rank.

clue.text: Inside empty briefcase, fit dry bread

indicators.note: the other letters go inside the outer letters
emptied of its middle, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: an ague is a fit of shivering fever
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: A dry bread roll inside an empty briefcase.
explanation.walkthrough: TT stands for teetotal, a crossword staple for dry.
explanation.definitionFit: A baguette is a long, thin French loaf.

clue.text: Down the bottom of chasm, nothing went up

indicators.note: the last letter, the bottom in a down entry

parts.note: O is the letter shaped like zero
rose means went up

explanation.surface: Down at the bottom of a chasm, nothing rose.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down means sullen and gloomy, which is morose.

clue.text: Grace introduces the first couple of enemies to friendship

indicators.note: the grace brings the letters into the other word
names the word they are put into

parts.note: amity is friendship

indicators.note: the first two letters of the word

explanation.surface: A gracious person introducing two enemies to friendship.
explanation.definitionFit: An amenity is a pleasant feature, a grace or nicety of life.

clue.text: Infernal god set to devour head of lady love

indicators.note: set eating up the letter places it inside

parts.note: to set is to put

indicators.note: the first letter of the word

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A hellish god preparing to eat the beloved.
explanation.definitionFit: Pluto was the Roman god of the underworld, ruler of the infernal regions.

clue.text: Right of leader in newspaper to support story

indicators.note: in a down entry, the support goes beneath

parts.note: a story is a lie, a fib

indicators.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: The right of the editor writing a newspaper leader to back a story.
explanation.definitionFit: A lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid.
